0.headline: Anthropic's Indian-origin CFO Krishna Rao's equity stake tops $700 million at proposed IPO price
0.heading: Anthropic's Indian-origin CFO Krishna Rao's equity stake tops $700 million at proposed IPO price
0.intro: Anthropic is seeking to raise as much as $90.4 billion at a potential valuation of about $1.4 trillion through its initial public offering and a private placement involving tech giants like Google and Microsoft.
0.body:
Just over two years after joining Anthropic as its first chief financial officer, Indian-origin executive Krishna Rao holds an equity stake in the artificial intelligence company valued at about $703 million, according to calculations based on its latest IPO filing.

Rao beneficially owns nearly 9.5 million shares, including shares underlying exercisable stock options, according to the filing. The estimate is based on the $74 midpoint of Anthropic's proposed IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share, before accounting for stock option exercise costs. Rao, however, is not selling any shares in the offering.

Known for maintaining a low public profile, Rao has been central to Anthropic's fundraising efforts and early IPO preparations. He is also playing an active role in the company's ongoing roadshow, meeting prospective investors at events hosted by Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs, ahead of its planned public market debut next week, according to The New York Times.

Other Indian-origin executives at Anthropic, including chief technology officer Rahul Patil, could also see substantial gains from what is poised to be one of the largest IPOs in history. However, Anthropic has not disclosed their individual equity holdings in its IPO filing.

Also Read: Anthropic S-1 filing decoded: Soaring revenue, voting structure, existential risks, and more

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI chatbot, is seeking to raise as much as $90.4 billion at a potential valuation of about $1.4 trillion through its initial public offering and a private placement involving technology giants including Google, Microsoft, AMD, Nvidia, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC.

Anthropic's seven co-founders, including chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, are set to sell shares worth about $250 million each in the IPO, taking their combined share sales to approximately $1.75 billion, while retaining stakes valued at roughly $18 billion apiece at the midpoint of the proposed price range.

Anthropic's IPO comes at a volatile moment for the technology sector, with a sharp selloff in AI-related stocks and growing concerns over the billions of dollars being poured into computing infrastructure.

Shifting political dynamics following the Democrats' recent electoral victories in the U.S. and the controversy involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang have added to the uncertainty in the sector.

1.headline: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in blockbuster IPO
1.heading: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in blockbuster IPO
1.intro: The Claude chatbot maker and some of its backers are seeking to raise as much as $90.4 billion in the IPO and a private placement
1.body:
Anthropic PBC is seeking a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion in its initial public offering, in a bid to make history as the first frontier artificial intelligence lab to go public.

The Claude chatbot maker and some of its backers are seeking to raise as much as $90.4 billion in the IPO and a private placement. The base offering would raise up to $64.4 billion, with shares marketed for $70 to $78 each, according to a filing on Tuesday with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Anthropic is offering 801.4 million shares, while backers are selling 23.6 million shares.

The figure also includes a private placement set to raise $26 billion in aggregate, to Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Broadcom Inc., Alphabet Inc.’s Google, Micron Technology Inc., Microsoft Corp., Nvidia Corp. and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., the filing shows.

At the top of the price range, Anthropic would have a market value of about $1 trillion, based on the shares outstanding listed in the filing. Accounting for employee stock options, restricted shares and stock reserved for the company’s charitable donation matching program, Anthropic would have a fully diluted value of about $1.4 trillion.

Anthropic’s ambitious target, including the private placement, would hit roughly $100 billion when including a so-called over-allotment option or greenshoe, Bloomberg News calculations show. That would top SpaceX’s $75 billion base offering, or the $86.2 billion it raised with the greenshoe.

The goal defies jitters from a sharp selloff in AI-related stocks last week, driven by expectations that politicians promising tougher regulation of data centers and related infrastructure will drive up costs and limit development of the technology.

Investors are under pressure to decide whether valuations in AI reflect a plausible trajectory for a technology that many expect to transform the economy and society as a whole, or overconfidence in an investment theme that hasn’t yet proven its staying power.

The widespread adoption of Claude Code and rival tools by software developers points to the potential transformation of a wide range of professional activity, from discovering new miracle drugs to navigating complex legal and accounting rules to running a factory. Already, more than 90% of contributions to Anthropic’s code base were written by Claude, the filing shows.

Anthropic has introduced so-called vertical solutions in these areas, with particular emphasis on healthcare and life sciences. It counts Novartis AG Chief Executive Officer Vas Narasimhan as one of its board members.

The IPO is set to price on Wednesday, Nov. 18, according to terms of the deal reviewed by Bloomberg.

Sales are surging. The company reported third-quarter revenue of nearly $17 billion as of Sept. 30, versus $1.4 billion in the same period a year ago, its filing shows. On Monday Anthropic unveiled new versions of its powerful Mythos and Fable models, both of which are faster than prior versions, while Fable is less expensive, as some companies cut back on their spending on the technology.

Keeping the pace of development running at a breakneck pace will require growing revenue faster than Anthropic’s spending on AI infrastructure. Anthropic has $895 billion of commitments, most of which are for computing power, chips, the filing shows. About $70 billion worth — a figure that’s larger than the individual market caps of roughly two-thirds of S&amp;P 500 companies — are due just in the year through September 2027.

Unlike other tech companies with sources of income such as advertising to fall back on, Anthropic will have to convince investors that its focus on AI alone will generate profit far beyond the technology’s surging costs. SpaceX may have tied its aspirations to AI when it pitched investors on its IPO, but most of its actual revenue at the time came from its other business lines.

That hasn’t stopped asset managers, venture capital firms and some of the biggest tech companies from backing Anthropic to the tune of tens of billions of dollars. Funds scattered across investment houses including Fidelity Investments, Capital Group and BlackRock Inc. and VCs such as Iconiq, Spark Capital and Sequoia Capital hold Anthropic shares before the IPO. Alphabet Inc.’s Google, Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. are backers as well as customers and key suppliers of computing power.

Pace the Frontier

The speed of development has become increasingly controversial, with Anthropic’s own Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei among those calling for top AI labs to “pace the frontier” in order to prioritize safety. Anthropic itself warned that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” in its IPO filing, if the technology isn’t developed with adequate safeguards and oversight.

Regulators, investors and even Anthropic’s employees have flagged the significant risk of humans losing control of the technology, with one putting the chance of AI eliminating all humans in the next decade at greater than 10%. Bill Gates said AI is powerful enough to drive events that cause “a billion deaths.”

Anthropic’s rival OpenAI is targeting a 2027 listing and Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman called 2026 an “ill-advised moment” for an IPO, citing concern over AI safety. The company is raising funds at a $1.25 trillion valuation, people familiar with the matter have said.

Anthropic’s origin story centers around former OpenAI executives defecting because they wanted to prioritize AI safety. Nearly six years after its founding, Anthropic has structured itself as a public benefit corporation that balances shareholder interests with those of society, and whose governance includes a Long-Term Benefit Trust that has the power to elect and remove a majority of the members of the company’s board.

Anthropic’s seven co-founders hold roughly 1.4% stakes in the company, making them each billionaires several times over. That remains true even if they stick to their pledges to give 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropic causes.

The company’s total operating expenses jumped to $17.5 billion in the third quarter, a 292% increase from a year prior. It flipped from an operating profit of $974 million in the second quarter — its first after at least five quarters of operating losses — back to a negative $567 million in the three months ended Sept. 30, according to the filing.

The operating loss in the third quarter was primarily driven by $5 billion of computing costs under short-term commitments and $2 billion of non-cash charges related to the company’s charitable donation-matching program.

AI pricing pressures have begun to hit Anthropic’s revenue. Lower prices on some of its new models, plus contractual discounts for some customers, reduced its revenue growth in the third quarter by about $600 million, the filing shows.

Anthropic has cut prices in newer model rollouts, including Opus 5.5 in September, and OpenAI has also introduced lower-priced models in recent months. The AI giants face growing competition from cheaper open-weight models, including from Chinese developers, which customers can download and fine-tune to their needs.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are leading Anthropic’s IPO, with participation from 20 other banks, the filing shows. The stock is expected to trade on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.
1.ai_impact_text_summary_s: Anthropic seeks to raise up to $90.4 billion in a record IPO and private placement targeting a $1 trillion valuation. Despite surging revenue and major tech backers, the AI lab faces immense infrastructure costs, safety risks, and rising competition.

* Major tech giants are participating in the $26B placement.

2.headline: Norwest Venture Partners and Kedaara Capital-backed Veritas Finance IPO gets SEBI nod
2.heading: Norwest Venture Partners and Kedaara Capital-backed Veritas Finance IPO gets SEBI nod
2.intro: Veritas Finance IPO | The professionally managed NBFC plans to raise Rs 900 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, while existing shareholders will sell up to 1.28 crore equity shares through an offer for sale.
2.body:
Veritas Finance, a Chennai-based non-banking financial company (NBFC), has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to proceed with its initial public offering (IPO).

The company, backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Kedaara Capital, refiled its draft IPO papers with the capital markets regulator on July 29, 2026, with a revised offer structure.

According to SEBI's processing status of draft offer documents published on November 9, the regulator issued its observations on Veritas Finance's draft prospectus on October 19, 2026.

The issuance of observations allows the company to proceed with the IPO process and file its red herring prospectus (RHP) with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), disclosing details such as the IPO opening dates and final issue structure.

The professionally managed NBFC plans to raise Rs 900 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, while existing shareholders will sell up to 1.28 crore equity shares through an offer for sale (OFS).

Investors Lok Capital Growth Fund and UK government-backed British International Investment plc, along with individuals D Arulmany, Growth Catalyst Partners LLC and Vidya Arulmany, will be among the selling shareholders in the OFS.

Earlier, Veritas Finance had filed its draft IPO papers in January 2025, aiming to raise up to Rs 2,800 crore through the public issue. Subsequently, SEBI approved the draft offer document in April 2025. However, the company did not proceed with its IPO plans at the time.

As part of the fresh issue, Veritas Finance may consider raising up to Rs 180 crore through a pre-IPO placement. If the company undertakes such a placement before filing the RHP with the RoC, the fresh issue size will be reduced accordingly.

The net proceeds from the fresh issue will be utilised to augment the company's capital base and meet future business requirements, including onward lending.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Norwest Venture Partners, with a 21.58 percent stake, is the largest shareholder in Veritas Finance, followed by Kedaara Capital Fund (15.08 percent), British International Investment (10.33 percent), and Lok Capital, founded by Rajiv Lall and Vishal Mehta, with a 9.48 percent stake.

Incorporated in 2015, Veritas Finance is a retail-focused NBFC primarily catering to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and self-employed individuals. It offers a range of financial products, including small business loans, housing loans, used commercial vehicle loans and working capital loans.

For the financial year ended March 2026, the company's net profit increased 12 percent year-on-year to Rs 330.4 crore, while net interest income (NII) rose 18 percent to Rs 1,133.5 crore, compared with the previous financial year.

The company's assets under management (AUM) increased 24.3 percent to Rs 9,134 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,348.6 crore in the previous year. Disbursements rose 16.4 percent to Rs 4,579.5 crore from Rs 3,933.1 crore during the same period.

Veritas Finance considers listed companies such as Five-Star Business Finance, SBFC Finance, Aavas Financiers, Aptus Value Housing Finance India and Sundaram Finance among its comparable peers.

ICICI Securities, IIFL Capital Services, JM Financial and SBI Capital Markets are the merchant bankers managing the Veritas Finance IPO.
